_what: C5 PLAN item b (user ruling 2026-11-22): reconcile covex-v6-state's dashcam on-time counts with its measured latency, by decomposing every monitor opportunity into seven exhaustive buckets
_denominator: one MONITOR OPPORTUNITY, one kind == 'monitor' row of outcomes.jsonl.gz, counted PER RUN. Verified equal to the committed scorer's sum of dashcam_per_device[*].n_instants on every cell with a score block. D153's pre-third-frame instants are already absent from it: the coordinator's epg.by_episode_index has no key below 2.
_delivery_rule_used: bucket on_time uses t_delivered (first token plus the per-row forward hop), which is what the committed scorer's _within reads and what outcomes.within_L records. The alternative D146 reading, delivery AT first token, is reported beside it as on_time_first_token_rule and is larger by exactly bucket late_at_forward_only.

_buckets.not_released: no request carries this opportunity_id; the coordinator never sent it
_buckets.released_unsettled: a request carries it, the outcome settled no delivery; a miss
_buckets.on_time: t_delivered - t_opportunity <= 1.0 s, THE COMMITTED RULE
_buckets.late_at_release: t_submit - t_opportunity > 1.0 s; the deadline was gone pre-engine
_buckets.late_at_first_token: released inside the deadline, first token outside it
_buckets.late_at_forward_only: first token inside, delivery outside; the D146 disagreement
_buckets.late_request_row_absent: late, settled, and with no request row to split; run-edge truncation of the request log

_proxies_declared.uplink: t_frame_arrive - t_opportunity, the trace's frame-arrival stamp, NOT a measured radio latency; ~0.06 s on every arm and seed, so it is a constant of the trace and carries no arm difference
_proxies_declared.coordinator_hold: t_submit - t_frame_arrive; bundles the arm's release decision with any queueing inside the coordinator and does not separate them
_proxies_declared.in_flight_occupancy: rebuilt from [t_submit, t_done] of requests carrying a monitor opportunity_id; an OCCUPANCY, not any arm's cap
_proxies_declared.not_a_proxy: why an instant is not_released. No per-opportunity refusal record exists in any log, so that bucket is not sub-attributed.

_caching: vLLM PREFIX CACHING WAS ENABLED in every cell read: non-zero vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total in the first metrics snapshot. Every latency here is a WARM-SERVER number under an arm-dependent hit pattern; none is a cold prefill. uncached = prompt_tokens - cached_tokens is reported beside it.

_excluded_held_code.why: covex-v6-state seeds 6 and 7 ran an unruled pricing switch and starved; they are NOT read by this script and must not be used for this reconciliation

denominator.unit: one monitor opportunity, counted PER RUN

control._claim: bucket on_time must EQUAL this cell's committed dashcam on-time count
control.committed_on_time_rule: an answer is delivered at COMPLETION, prefill plus decode (D146, the default from 2026-11-20); a dashcam Yes/No stays at first token

d146_both_readings.note: the committed cell uses t_delivered, which for a monitor is first token plus the forward hop; the first-token reading is also what the coordinator's own cloud_payload.on_time flag records

late_at_first_token_stratified._why: late_at_first_token is NOT a bucket of slow engine work. These rows are late because the deadline runs from t_opportunity while the engine's clock starts at t_submit, and at covex-v6-state most of the deadline is gone by then.
late_at_first_token_stratified._register_of_the_last_two: CONSTRUCTED BOUND, not an observed count. 'engine service within the whole deadline' says the server's own time would have fitted inside 1.0 s had release been instantaneous. Release cannot be instantaneous: the uplink alone is ~0.06 s, and holding none of these requests would change the queue they were served in, so the server time itself would not be preserved. It bounds how much of this bucket the RELEASE side could in principle reach; it predicts no arm's result.

late_split_release_vs_engine._ruling: USER RULING 2026-11-22: split every LATE monitor by whether the deadline was lost BEFORE submission or after it. The three components are differences of consecutive stamps on one clock, so release_delay + engine_time + forward_hop = t_delivered - t_opportunity identically.

partition._identity: by construction this partition IS the three late buckets renamed: deadline_already_lost_at_release == late_at_release, lost_by_release_plus_engine == late_at_first_token, and lost_only_by_the_forward_hop == late_at_forward_only. It is computed independently and checked, so an equality here is a CONSISTENCY CHECK on the two code paths and NOT new evidence

c5_trip_classes._question: part (3) of the ruling: which SLOW monitors trip C5, by what their wait overlapped. A monitor TRIPS C5 when its first token, measured from t_submit, exceeds 0.8 x L_dash = 0.8 s, which is the AIMD trip whose reconstruction in c5_loss_split.py reproduced the base arm's own c5_decrease / c5_increase counters
c5_trip_classes._population: LATE monitors only, which is the population the ruling asks about; a tripping monitor that still delivered on time is not in it
c5_trip_classes._precedence_note: the PARTITION assigns a monitor overlapping several classes to the first of recall, build_piece, touch, so the four classes sum to n_tripping. The non-exclusive counts are given beside it because a precedence order is a choice and the reader should be able to see past it

all_released_thresholds._population: ALL released monitors, late or not. This is the population the user's own reference measurement is over, so these are the numbers that compare directly with it; the late-only figures are in late_split_release_vs_engine

diagnostics_for_not_released._register: DIAGNOSTIC, not an attribution. The logs carry no refusal record keyed to an opportunity, so bucket not_released is never sub-attributed.

settled_deliveries_with_no_request_row.note: the request log is truncated at the run edge relative to the outcomes; these instants are scored on t_delivered alone and their latency components are not available

prefix_caching.label: WARM SERVER: every latency in this cell was served with prefix caching on; none of these numbers is a cold prefill

traced_unit_median_release_delay._why: one traced unit, a late_at_first_token instant, arithmetic by hand
traced_unit_median_release_delay.bound_by: release_delay consumed 82% of the 1.0 s deadline, then the engine's own first token needed 0.751 s more

cells.traced_unit_note: the MEDIAN-release-delay row of the late_at_first_token bucket, chosen so the trace is representative of the bucket rather than of its tail; uplink + hold + ttft + forward_hop must equal delivered_age to the rounding shown

answer._dominance_is_reported_per_cell: covex-v6-state's two usable seeds do NOT share a dominant bucket: seed 4 is not_released (5,397 of 11,764) and seed 5 is late_at_first_token (5,641 of 11,769), and seed 4 is also the cell that exhausted its 1,200 GPU-second budget exactly and logged 12,824 budget refusals while seed 5 spent 1,066.77 s and logged none. Pooling the two would name one bucket and hide that the two seeds are in different regimes.
answer.c5_trip_classes_reading: PLAINLY, AND IT IS THE FAVOURABLE ANSWER rather than the feared one: the NONE class is SMALL. At the repriced rung-2 cell 93 of 944 tripping late monitors, 9.9 percent, trip C5 with nothing of ours in flight, and 139 of 841 at the repriced seed 5, 16.5 percent; at seed 4 the other 90.1 percent overlap a recall (702, 74.4 percent), a build piece (93, 9.9 percent) or a touch (56, 5.9 percent). The same shape holds on every cell: NONE is 9.9 to 22.8 percent, and recall overlap is the largest class everywhere (70 to 88 percent). So a C5 attribution rule has a reachable path on about 9 in 10 of the halvings, and the irreducible residue it cannot suppress is bounded at roughly 10 to 23 percent of trips, cell-dependent. TWO LIMITS ON THIS, both stated rather than buried: overlap is CO-OCCURRENCE IN TIME, not a proven causal wait, and with 2,466 touch intervals spanning the run a co-occurrence is cheap, which is why the non-exclusive counts are published beside the precedence partition; and NONE being small bounds what the rule could reach among TRIPS, not how much on-time it would recover, because the halving is only one input to the hold.
answer.reading: The first-token distribution cannot see the loss because the deadline is measured from t_opportunity and the first-token figure is measured from t_submit. At covex-v6-state the gap between those two stamps is the whole story: the median release delay is 0.73 to 0.74 s of a 1.0 s deadline, and 40 percent of released monitors are already past 0.8 s old when the engine first sees them. A 0.49 s median first token on top of that lands the median delivery at 1.22 s, so a monitor that was fast by every engine measure still misses. The uplink is ~0.06 s and identical across arms; the forward hop is the 0.0222 s constant; so the release delay is coordinator HOLD, and it is 0.68 s at covex-v6-state against 0.24 s at the base. On top of that, covex-v6-state never releases 29 to 46 percent of its monitor opportunities at all. THE TWO REPRICED CELLS SETTLE THE ATTRIBUTION: covex-v6-state-uo seeds 4 and 5 both have ZERO budget refusals, so budget starvation cannot be the explanation there, and both show the same picture - release delay p50 0.742 and 0.724 s against the base's 0.300 s, 71.6 and 71.3 percent of released monitors over 0.5 s against 37.1 percent, and 71.2 and 70.0 percent with release plus first token already over the whole 1.0 s deadline against 36.7 percent - while the engine does the SAME WORK on every arm (dashcam uncached median 376 against 374, so episodes are not being evicted) and first token moves only 0.44 to 0.48 s at p50. Lateness at rung 2 is a coordinator RELEASE decision, not engine time.

repricing_comparison._two_different_objects_do_not_conflate: the `by_deadline` headline quoted for these cells is the ROBOT pool metric, `robot_headline.correct_answers_delivered_by_deadline`, over 127 to 132 QUESTIONS. The dashcam decomposition in this file is a DIFFERENT object over ~11,769 monitor INSTANTS. They are reported in separate rows and must not be compared with each other or summed.
repricing_comparison._register_warning: READ THESE AS SINGLE SEEDS WITH NO INTERVAL. There are two repriced cells, one per seed, so no dispersion can be computed and NO DIRECTION IS SUPPORTED by either difference on its own. Specifically, the seed-5 robot difference of -0.0079 is ONE QUESTION out of 127 (55 correct against 54): it is not a regression and must not be presented as one. The seed-4 difference of +0.1061 is 14 questions out of 132. The budget state is why the two differ and this analysis CONFIRMS that account from the logs: the old-price seed-4 cell exhausted its 1,200 GPU-second budget EXACTLY (1,200.0 of 1,200.0) and logged 12,824 budget refusals, while the old-price seed-5 cell spent 1,066.77 s and logged NONE. A charge fix can only bite where the charge bound, so a large seed-4 move and a one-question seed-5 move is the expected shape rather than a conflict. Both repriced cells have ZERO budget refusals (1,191.41 and 1,177.69 of 1,200.0 spent), which is what makes them the first rung-2 cells whose dashcam numbers are attributable to SCHEDULING alone. On the dashcam object this file decomposes, both seeds move the same way (+517 and +60 instants), and the +60 is likewise too small for a single seed to carry.
